profile.name: Neha Seth
profile.title: Frontend Engineer
profile.tagline: 10+ years building consumer-facing web apps — the last three on payments and checkout, where every pixel touches money.
profile.hook: I like the parts of the frontend nobody sees until they break: payment flows across nine markets, error taxonomies that page the right team, and the conversion review that turns a 0.4% drop into next sprint's work.
profile.availability: Open to Senior Frontend roles — Netherlands, EU or remote
profile.workEligibility: Eligible to work full-time in the Netherlands

experience.blurb: Global online food delivery marketplace in 20+ countries. Payments and checkout for the consumer web platform.
highlights: Integrated 15 payment methods across nine European markets — Apple Pay, Google Pay, Amazon Pay, PayPal, iDEAL and local bank schemes — covering saved cards, recurring payments and market-specific rules.
Founded a new payments frontend service as its first engineer: chose the stack, built the repository and CI foundations, and shipped the first release behind a feature flag.
Owned payment error monitoring for web: built the logging taxonomy mapping frontend payment failures to DataDog dashboards and alerts, aligned with iOS so both platforms alert consistently.
Led the team's recurring payment-conversion review — success rates by market, method and device — turning drops into prioritised engineering work.
Diagnosed and fixed high-impact checkout defects across frontend and backend, including an Apple Pay / Google Pay total-amount mismatch and a race condition that blocked Apple Pay for iOS 18 users.
Delivered features at scale with feature flags and A/B experiments, instrumenting analytics to measure payment-option and voucher behaviour in production.
Retired three legacy payment code paths without regressing checkout; wrote the checkout architecture review and onboarding docs now used across the department.
Built partner-facing invoicing — search, filters, bulk export, invoice preview — in a Vue 3 micro-frontend on a shared component library.

experience.blurb: Vulnerability management platform helping companies find and fix security gaps in their infrastructure.
highlights: Developed and maintained React web interfaces for Greenbone's vulnerability management products in a cross-functional team.
Partnered with backend and product engineers on API integration and application performance across the product surface.

experience.blurb: One of Germany's largest online comparison portals for consumer loans.
highlights: Built the homepage and landing pages from scratch in React, Next.js and TypeScript, and maintained them in a cross-functional team.
Owned the offer stage of the loan application journey — the conversion-critical step where users compare and select a loan offer.
Acted as process lead for the team, coordinating initiatives with management and dependent teams.
Maintained a domain of interconnected projects together with the development and infrastructure tooling around them.

experience.blurb: Berlin fintech giving consumers free access to their credit score and financial data.
highlights: Built the customer-facing web application in React and parts of the mobile application in React Native.
Translated design templates into responsive, accessible UI as the frontend owner of assigned features.
Integrated REST APIs in an agile, microservice-based environment, coordinating with backend teams on contract changes.

experience.blurb: Joined as an intern and was promoted to Junior Frontend Developer within the year.
highlights: Contributed to the consumer web application in React, JavaScript, HTML and CSS.
Delivered UI features from design templates in a Scrum team, collaborating with design and backend engineers.

education.note: Component architecture, state management, React Native.

beforeTech: Before moving to Berlin in 2016, Neha taught computer applications at educational institutions in India — which is where the habit of writing onboarding docs people actually read comes from.

paymentMethods.name: Credit / debit card
paymentMethods.story: The baseline every market shares. Hosted Adyen fields keep PAN data out of our DOM; 3DS2 challenges render in an iframe and the result is reconciled against the order total before confirmation.

paymentMethods.name: Saved card
paymentMethods.flow: Tokenised stored credential, CVC-less where the scheme allows
paymentMethods.story: Stored credentials are where conversion lives: one tap instead of sixteen digits. The tricky part is market-specific rules — some schemes require CVC re-entry, some don't — encoded once and tested per market in Playwright.

paymentMethods.name: Recurring / subscription
paymentMethods.flow: Merchant-initiated transactions on a stored token
paymentMethods.story: Subscriptions mean merchant-initiated transactions with no shopper present, so the initial consent flow has to capture exactly the right recurringProcessingModel or the renewals fail silently weeks later.

paymentMethods.name: Apple Pay
paymentMethods.flow: Payment sheet, merchant validation, token decryption server-side
paymentMethods.story: Two production bugs live here. A total-amount mismatch between the payment sheet and the order (fixed by deriving the sheet total from the same source as the order summary), and a race condition that blocked Apple Pay entirely on iOS 18 — the sheet was requested before merchant validation settled. Toggle the iOS 18 device to see the fix.

paymentMethods.name: Google Pay
paymentMethods.story: Shares the total-amount fix with Apple Pay. isReadyToPay gates the button so users never see a wallet they can't use — a small thing that removed a whole class of 'button does nothing' support tickets.

paymentMethods.name: Amazon Pay
paymentMethods.flow: Hosted button → Amazon checkout session → return URL
paymentMethods.story: A redirect flow with a twist: the return URL must rehydrate the entire checkout state, including vouchers and tips. Built as a resumable state machine so a round-trip through Amazon lands the user exactly where they left.

paymentMethods.name: PayPal
paymentMethods.flow: Smart button, popup approval, server capture
paymentMethods.story: Popup-based approval that has to survive Safari's popup blocker and users switching tabs mid-flow. Instrumented every exit path so a closed popup logs as an abandon, not an error.

paymentMethods.name: iDEAL
paymentMethods.story: The Dutch default. The redirect result page can arrive before the webhook, so the UI polls payment status with backoff and renders a calm 'confirming with your bank' state instead of a false failure.

paymentMethods.name: Bancontact
paymentMethods.flow: Card-like scheme, app or card, redirect-confirmed
paymentMethods.story: Belgium's card scheme that behaves like a bank redirect on mobile. The mobile flow deep-links into the bank app and back, so the checkout has to be re-entrant.

paymentMethods.name: Payconiq
paymentMethods.flow: QR on desktop, app deep-link on mobile
paymentMethods.story: Same company as Bancontact, opposite UX: a QR code on desktop and an app switch on mobile. Device detection decides which to render, and the QR refreshes before it expires.

paymentMethods.name: EPS
paymentMethods.story: Austria's online bank transfer. The issuer list changes, so it's fetched at runtime rather than hardcoded — one of the market-specific rules that made the config-driven approach pay off.

paymentMethods.name: Twint
paymentMethods.story: Switzerland's mobile wallet. CHF rounding rules (to 0.05) surfaced a display mismatch between the sheet and the order summary — the same class of bug as the Apple Pay total, caught by a multi-market Playwright suite.

paymentMethods.name: Dankort
paymentMethods.flow: Domestic Danish card, co-branded with Visa
paymentMethods.story: Co-branded cards mean the BIN can route to Dankort or Visa; the checkout has to present the right brand logo and fee disclosure, which is regulated in Denmark.

paymentMethods.name: Open Banking
paymentMethods.story: UK account-to-account payments. Low fees, but the consent journey is long; measured drop-off per step in the conversion review and shortened the bank picker with recently-used banks first.

paymentMethods.name: Meal voucher
paymentMethods.flow: Voucher balance covers eligible items, remainder on another method
paymentMethods.story: Split payments: vouchers only cover eligible items, so the order summary has to explain why €4.20 is left over and offer a second method for it. Instrumented voucher usage with Snowplow to measure how often the split confuses people.
